title: Graceful Degradation Matrix & UX Decision Notes for Rollouts
content:
Context: working through UX decisions for how the console should present and execute graceful degradation (automatic fallback, canary -> full, A/B experiments) when model or infra regressions occur. This doc captures a decision matrix, microcopy variants, quick wireframe notes, and a short operator checklist for on-call.

High-level goals (product constraints):
- Make it obvious which policy is active for a route (manual, canary, A/B, auto-fallback).
- Show health signals that matter to decisions: user-facing error rate, model quality delta (evals/prompt set), latency p50/p95, cost per token.
- Prefer automated, least-surprising fallbacks that are reversible and auditable.
- Surface why a fallback happened (primary signal + correlated metrics) in plain language.

Decision matrix (failure mode -> UX + action):
- High client error rate (>1.5% 5m rolling) with stable latency: UX - large yellow banner on route, "Automatic fallback: model X -> baseline" CTA to rollback. Action - auto-fallback to baseline model variant; mark rollout as "paused". Rationale - prioritize correctness over perf.
- Latency spike (p95 > 2s above baseline): UX - non-blocking advisory pill, show p50/p95 trend sparkline next to model card; suggest enabling burst pool or enabling smaller-quantized variant. Action - default: route to lower-latency variant if configured; otherwise nudge operator.
- Quality regression detected (eval set A, BLEU/ROUGE/token-level checks): UX - red badge on canary cohort, inline summary: "Quality delta: -7% on safety prompts"; provide link to sample diffs and first-failure example. Action - automatic rollback to previous stable model; do not promote.
- Partial capacity failure (zone down, degraded throughput): UX - small amber banner with region-level notice; allow traffic re-route UI (button: "Redirect traffic to region eu-west1"). Action - auto-fallback to cross-region variant if policy permits; otherwise surface manual reroute.

Wireframe + interaction notes (left-to-right console flow):
- Left rail: Routes list -> selected route shows active rollout state (big pill: CANARY 10% -> 90% progress).
- Top header of route detail: primary metric strip (errors, p95, quality delta, cost) with colored chips (green/amber/red).
- Main canvas: two tabs: "Rollout config" and "Observability". Rollout config shows current policy (editable): traffic split, promotion rules, fallback policy. Observability shows time-series + first-class sample diffs.
- Right rail (compact): quick-ops (pause rollout, force promote, force rollback), recent audit events, and a single-click "Simulate fallback" that replays last 30m of traffic against fallback target for quick sanity checks.
- In-canary controls: slider to adjust % (0.1% granularity for low-volume routes), schedule button (ramp to X over Y minutes), and a confidence threshold toggle (requires N successful eval checks).

Microcopy suggestions (variants to test):
- Fallback banner variants:
  1) "Automatic fallback engaged: traffic routed to Stable‑v2. Learn why" (concise, action-first)
  2) "We detected a quality regression. To protect users we switched to Stable‑v2. View samples →" (explanatory, empathy)
  3) "Fallback triggered by error-rate threshold (1.5%). Override? [Resume rollout] [View details]" (operator-forward)
- Confirmation dialog copy for forced rollback:
  - Title: "Force rollback to Stable‑v2"
  - Body: "Rolling back will redirect 100% of traffic to Stable‑v2 and pause the current rollout. This action is reversible but will trigger a new audit event. Proceed?"

Operator checklist for on-call (short, actionable):
- Check route header metrics (errors, p95, quality delta).
- If fallback occurred, open audit event -> reason -> sample diffs. Share link in incident slack thread.
- If latency spike: attempt simulate fallback to lower-latency variant (right rail). If simulation ok, apply fallback.
- If capacity shortage: consider temporary traffic redirection and escalate infra.

Backlog and open questions (grooming items):
- UX: Add "why this threshold" tooltip for each auto-fallback trigger (link to org SLOs).
- Product: define canonical set of quality signals we accept for auto-fallback (e.g., eval delta > 5% AND failure samples > 3).
- Infra: implement a cheap deterministic simulator for "simulate fallback" (replay recent requests w/ cached keys). Who owns? SRE + serving-runtime.
- Engineering: slider granularity for low-volume routes — we need throttled ramping to prevent thrash.
- Security/legal: audit copy must include request-id hashing policy for privacy.

Edge cases and scenarios to test (manual and automated):
- Canary with long-tail latency: small % of users see slow responses but metrics are within threshold — how do we avoid noisy rollbacks? Proposed: require 3 consecutive windows before auto-fallback.
- A/B swap that changes semantic behavior (answers are correct but different tone): difficult to detect with perf metrics; add "human eval review" trigger for major model changes.
- Multi-variant fallbacks: fallback target unavailable -> fallback to next-available compatible variant, or pause rollout. UX should make the chain visible (breadcrumb).

Quick simulation plan for next sprint (MVP):
1) Implement top-line banner + chips (errors, p95, quality delta) in route view.
2) Add a single auto-fallback policy: "error-rate > 1.5% for 5m -> fallback to baseline" with audit event and banner copy variant A.
3) Build a "simulate fallback" button that replays last 10m requests to a specified target in a sandbox (no billing).
4) Add microcopy A/B experiment for banner variant and confirmation dialog.

Notes-to-self / low-priority ideas:
- Could we include a short natural-language explanation of the metric delta ("errors rose 2.3x due to tokenization change") using an automated insight generator? Risk: hallucination.
- Consider a "safety net" toggle for orgs that want manual-only fallbacks (enterprise).
- Add keyboard shortcut to pause current rollout (for power users) — nice-to-have.

Open action items (owners):
- Devon: prototype the route header chips + banner (eta 2025-01-28).
- Elena: draft microcopy variants and run small user test with solutions team (eta 2025-01-24).
- Ravi: scope simulate-fallback backend requirements with serving-runtime (eta 2025-01-30).

References + inspiration:
- "Canary deployments at scale" internal talk — Confluence link above.
- Existing rollout playbook (see linked artifacts).

Unresolved tradeoffs we should discuss in review:
- Silent auto-fallback vs explicit notification cadence (do we page on fallback?). Proposed: only page on critical infra events; notify via banner + audit otherwise.
- Degree of explanation in the banner (too much detail could confuse non-technical PMs).

End notes: this doc is intentionally pragmatic — we want small, testable increments that improve operator confidence without overwhelming the UI. Keep the next PR scoped to metric chips + one fallback policy + microcopy A/B.

-- Maya (notes from product working session, 2025-01-12)
